Frequently Asked Questions

My commercial door won't close properly — can it be repaired or does it need to be replaced?

In most cases, a commercial door that won't close properly can be repaired. The most common causes are hinge wear, frame shift, or a failing closer — all of which are repairable. We diagnose the specific issue first and give you a clear recommendation before any work starts. If the frame has shifted beyond what adjustment can correct or the door has structural damage, we'll tell you replacement makes more sense.

How quickly can you respond to a commercial door problem in Charlotte?

We schedule commercial door repairs quickly — typically within a few days for standard repairs. For situations where the door is non-functional or creating a security issue, call us directly at (704) 771-6111 and we'll discuss priority scheduling.

Can you replace the glass panel in a commercial door without replacing the entire door?

Yes, in most cases. If the door frame is in good condition and the door itself is structurally sound, we can replace just the broken glass panel. We source tempered safety glass cut to the correct specification for the door and install it without disturbing the surrounding frame.

How long do commercial door closers last?

Commercial door closer lifespan depends heavily on traffic volume. On a high-traffic commercial entry — a busy retail or restaurant door — closers may need replacement every 5–10 years. Lower-traffic entries last longer. Signs that a closer is failing include a door that swings too fast or too slow, doesn't close completely, or slams shut. We replace closers with units rated for the door's traffic volume.

Do you service commercial doors for property management companies?

Yes. We work with property managers overseeing commercial properties in Charlotte. We can handle door maintenance, repair, and replacement across multiple locations and work within your existing service request and documentation process.

My commercial door hardware keeps failing — is this a hardware quality issue or an installation issue?

It can be either. Commercial door hardware that fails repeatedly is often a specification problem — residential-grade or incorrectly rated hardware installed on a commercial door that sees more use than the hardware was designed for. It can also be an installation issue. We diagnose the root cause and specify replacement hardware correctly for the door's use requirements so the repair holds.
